items: Brent settles 8.7% lower at $94.62 on Wednesday, its first close under $100 since September, after Vance blames the midterm defeat on the Iran war → markets bet Washington wants out of the war; oil down more than 14% this week sharply cuts Egypt's fuel and LNG import bill.
The pound gains 65 piasters in one session to EGP 54.77 per dollar at the CBE → falling oil and the 100 bp hike ease dollar demand; a stronger pound lowers import costs and inflation pressure.

EGX30 jumps 2.83% to 50,650.18, back above 50,000, as 197 stocks rise and foreign institutions net buy EGP 338.7 mn → peace hopes, cheaper oil and a firmer pound pull foreign money back; pharma and consumer names lead.

Iran calls the US reply to its Hormuz plan unconvincing but Qatar says both sides stay committed, and Trump tells the FT he has no immediate plans to strike → talks continue despite attacks on shipping, keeping a deal and lower energy costs in play for Egypt.
The EBRD, the IFC and Helikon each disclose about 6.9% of Banque du Caire after buying EGP 16.7 bn of shares at EGP 5.30 → anchor foreign holders give the new listing a stable shareholder base.

Democrats win both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, with CNBC projecting at least 245 House seats and at least 51 in the Senate → a divided Washington constrains Trump's agenda for the rest of his term, including war spending, as talks with Iran continue.

EGX30 rebounds 1.76% to 49,255.66 on Tuesday, ending a four-session fall, as 180 stocks rise and foreigners net buy about EGP 130 mn → a firmer pound and lower oil bring back foreign buyers; developers and Eastern Company lead while fertiliser names fall.

Gas supplies to fertilizer plants are cut 20% while Egyptian urea sells at $535 a ton, about 17% above September → LNG cargoes now cost over $100 mn each, so the state rations gas; Abu Qir confirms the cut and falls 3.59%.

Brent settles 1% lower at $103.60, its lowest close since 7 October, as traders weigh US-Iran talks → Iran calls the US reply unconvincing, but Qatar expects both sides' feedback within 36 hours; lower oil eases Egypt's import bill.

The government weighs selling a large EgyptAlum stake on the EGX before year-end, after Banque du Caire raised $658 mn → the state targets $1.5 bn of offerings this year; a new listing would add depth for brokers and investors.

Brent falls 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday, its biggest drop in three months, after Iran's supreme leader approves talks and Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz in two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound, though a US strike on Qeshm Island overnight lifts Brent 0.5% in Asia.

The pound strengthens to EGP 55.51 per dollar at the CBE on Monday from 56.12 after the hike, and major banks quote 55.49 → the 100 bp hike and falling oil ease demand for dollars; a firmer pound helps importers and foreign holders of local debt.

EGX30 slips 0.70% to 48,403.14 while the EGX70 and EGX100 fall more than 2.2% and 197 stocks decline against 31 → foreigners net sell EGP 138.1 mn and Banque du Caire absorbs 21% of turnover, leaving little cash for small caps.

Banque du Caire closes its first session at EGP 5.31, up 0.19% on the EGP 5.30 offer, after touching EGP 5.68 → pricing at fair value leaves little first-day gain; the Treasury takes up to half the EGP 36.37 bn proceeds to ease debt.

Egypt's non-oil PMI stays at 47.2 in October, below a 48 forecast and its tenth straight month below 50 → output and new orders fall at the fastest pace in four months and input costs rise at a five-month high.

EGX30 falls 1.72% to 48,744.01 in the first session after the hike, with 148 stocks down and only 63 up as Palm Hills drops 7% → higher rates hit developers and consumer lenders while foreign and Arab investors sell; turnover of EGP 7.2 bn is 35% below its 90-day average.

Banque du Caire starts trading today as BQDC at an offer price of EGP 5.30, after a record EGP 205.8 bn of private-placement orders → the debut tests demand in a falling market; retail holders can sell back at EGP 5.30 for 30 days through CI Capital.

The state borrows about EGP 4.3 tn at home in July to October, almost all to refinance, and a finance official says the hike adds EGP 150 bn to the bill → short-dated debt reprices fast, so the 100 bp move feeds straight into the budget; the first post-hike 364-day bill sells at 26.076%.

Brent falls about 3.2% to $109.75 early Monday after Iran says a Qatari-brokered plan could reopen Hormuz within two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's import bill, but Trump still talks of hitting one or two more targets after Tuesday's midterms.

AMOC reports quarterly sales up 41% to EGP 43.2 bn and net profit up 154% to EGP 3.475 bn → high oil prices and refining margins lift results; the stock rises 2.21% on Sunday against a falling market.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Iran says Hormuz stays shut and there are no nuclear talks until the US meets its demands, as one report says US strikes could come as early as 4 November → the risk of a wider war after the midterms keeps oil, shipping and regional risk premiums high as the EGX reopens.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The pound holds at EGP 56.12 per dollar at the CBE as banks open Sunday at 56.04–56.19 to sell, the first quotes after the hike → the hike has not yet moved the pound, so today's EGX session tests how equities price higher rates.

stories.h: EGX30 rises for a third day to 51,153 as market cap passes EGP 4 tn
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; See News; Youm7; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Thursday at 51,152.73, up 0.99%; the EGX70 rises 2.42% and the EGX100 1.96%. 169 stocks rise and 40 fall, market cap gains about EGP 61 bn to EGP 4.05 tn, and turnover is about EGP 10.2 bn. Palm Hills (+5.7%), Heliopolis Housing (+5.0%) and Raya Holding (+2.8%) lead, while Edita (-3.0%) and Qalaa (-1.8%) fall. Foreigners net buy EGP 211.9 mn while Egyptians and Arabs sell.
stories.why: None of the sources gives a single cause; the gains come as the pound firms and foreign investors buy both stocks and bills.
stories.aff: Foreign-held blue chips, developers and small caps.
stories.eg: EnterpriseAM puts the EGX30 up 22.3% year to date.
stories.egx: Bullish across the market; consumer names take some profit.
stories.names: Palm Hills, Heliopolis Housing, Raya, CIB (up); Edita, Qalaa (down).

key.l: CBE sell rate, EGP per USD, Thu 5 Nov evening

stories.h: Pound strengthens to 54.01 as foreigners return to Egyptian T-bills
stories.src: El Balad; Cairo Mubasher; Middle East Observer
stories.what: The CBE quotes 53.87 buy and 54.01 sell on Thursday evening, El Balad reports, after a 54.77 close on Wednesday. National Bank of Egypt and Banque Misr quote 53.87 and 53.97. Foreign and Arab investors net buy $112.3 mn of T-bills in the secondary market on Wednesday, after $196.4 mn on Tuesday, the Middle East Observer says.
stories.why: Falling oil and the 26% bill yields after the CBE's hike draw carry-trade money back.
stories.aff: Import costs, inflation expectations, foreign holders of local debt and companies with dollar debt.
stories.eg: A stronger pound cuts the cost of imported fuel, wheat and inputs and eases inflation pressure.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers, banks and foreign-held blue chips; mildly bearish for exporters.

key.l: net international reserves, end-October, a record

stories.h: Reserves hit a record $57.5 bn at end-October
stories.what: The CBE says net international reserves reach about $57.5 bn at the end of October, up about $152 mn or 0.27% from about $57.35 bn in September, according to provisional data released on Thursday. Amwal Al Ghad calls it a record.
stories.why: Reserves keep rising despite foreign selling of local debt in late October; the sources do not break down the drivers.
stories.aff: The pound, Egypt's import cover and its credit standing.
stories.eg: A larger buffer gives the CBE room to smooth the pound as the IMF's final review approaches.
stories.egx: Bullish for sentiment toward Egyptian assets.

stories.h: Brent rebounds 3.9% to $98.29 as tanker attacks resume
stories.what: Brent settles $3.67 higher at $98.29 and WTI $2.40 higher at $90.52, after both fell more than 8% on Wednesday to their lowest since 31 August. UKMTO reports at least five vessels hit since Sunday, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two tankers and a tugboat catch fire after using unauthorised routes. UBS's Paul Donovan sees oil worth $80 to $85 a barrel once fighting ends, The National reports.
stories.why: Traders are wary of pricing a quick return to normal flows before diplomacy delivers safe shipping.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel and LNG import bill, the pound and inflation.
stories.eg: Oil near $100 still costs Egypt far more than before the war, even after this week's fall.
stories.egx: Mildly bearish for importers and energy users after Wednesday's relief.

key.l: conditions Iran sets before reopening Hormuz

stories.h: Iran says Hormuz stays shut until the US meets all seven conditions
stories.what: A senior Iranian official tells Reuters the two sides remain far apart. Tehran wants oil sanctions waived, the US naval blockade lifted and frozen funds released before Hormuz reopens, with nuclear talks only after that. Qatar leads mediation and expects feedback within 36 hours, while Trump says the US is ready to strike but may not need to.
stories.why: Both sides keep talking after the US midterms while attacks on shipping continue.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: A reopened Hormuz would ease Egypt's energy costs and help a Suez recovery.

week.why: The first inflation print after the CBE's 100 bp hike; September urban inflation was 13.9%. CAPMAS usually publishes around the 9th or 10th.
